idiom_name: Hibernate/JPA persistence context via EntityManager on the JVM
implementation_notes: Kotlin persistence on the JVM inherits the JPA persistence context: EntityManager.find returns the managed instance for an identity and merge copies state onto it, so the classic keyed map is replaced by the EntityManager/Spring Data repository lifecycle - keep one manager (or one transactional context) per unit of work and bound it with clear()/detach(). Pure Kotlin SQL frameworks such as Exposed do not expose a session identity map, so there the map must be hand-rolled in the repository. Prefer the JPA context when the stack already uses Hibernate and do not add a second map beside it.
code_sketch:
val em = emf.createEntityManager()
em.transaction.begin()
val a = em.find(Customer::class.java, 42L)
val b = em.find(Customer::class.java, 42L)
check(a === b)                 // same managed instance
em.transaction.commit()
em.close()
pitfalls: Kotlin data classes derive equals()/hashCode() from constructor properties: comparing entities by value confuses identity with structural equality, and mutable properties make them unsafe map keys - key on the typed id instead.
A long-lived application-managed EntityManager is a stale, growing cache; close it per transaction or request.
EntityManager is not thread-safe: suspend functions must not share one manager across coroutines or dispatchers.
